content: The solubility of ledipasvir decreases as gastric pH increases. Drugs that elevate gastric pH are expected to reduce the levels of ledipasvir. To mitigate this interaction, antacids and ledipasvir/sofosbuvir should be administered at least 4 hours apart. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases colchicine levels or effects via inhibition of the P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter. The use of colchicine with P-gp inhibitors is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. If coadministration is necessary, the colchicine dose or frequency should be reduced as per prescribing information. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases dabigatran levels or effects via P-gp inhibition. For atrial fibrillation, avoid coadministration if creatinine clearance (CrCl) is less than 30 mL/min. For deep vein thrombosis (DVT) or pulmonary embolism (PE) treatment, avoid coadministration if CrCl is less than 50 mL/min. Danicopan increases the plasma concentrations of P-gp substrates, including ledipasvir/sofosbuvir. Dose reduction of P-gp substrates should be considered where even minimal concentration changes may lead to serious adverse reactions. Darolutamide, a breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) inhibitor, increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels or effects. Avoid coadministration with BCRP inhibitors. If unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider dose reduction of BCRP substrate drugs. Dexlansoprazole decreases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels due to increased gastric pH. Proton pump inhibitor (PPI) doses comparable to omeprazole 20 mg or less can be administered simultaneously with ledipasvir/sofosbuvir under fasted conditions. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases digoxin levels or effects via P-gp inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases duvelisib levels or effects via P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases edoxaban levels or effects via P-gp inhibition. Dose adjustment may be required with strong P-gp inhibitors. For DVT/PE treatment, reduce the edoxaban dose to 30 mg orally once daily. No dose reduction is recommended for nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF). Elagolix increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels or effects via P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF levels via P-gp inhibition. Tenofovir levels may increase, necessitating dose regimen adjustments. Enasidenib increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels or effects via inhibition of organic anion-transporting polypeptides (OATP1B1/3) and BCRP. Avoid coadministration with sensitive OATP1B1/3 or BCRP substrates. If unavoidable, reduce the substrate dosage as per prescribing information. Encorafenib, a BCRP inhibitor, increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels or effects. Monitor for signs of increased exposure and consider dose adjustments of BCRP substrates. Erdafitinib increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels or effects via P-gp inhibition. If coadministration is unavoidable, separate administration by at least 6 hours before or after P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. Esomeprazole decreases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels due to increased gastric pH. PPI doses comparable to omeprazole 20 mg or less can be administered simultaneously with ledipasvir/sofosbuvir under fasted conditions. Famotidine decreases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels due to increased gastric pH. H2-receptor antagonists may be administered simultaneously or 12 hours apart from ledipasvir/sofosbuvir at doses not exceeding famotidine 40 mg twice daily. Fosphenytoin decreases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via P-gp induction. This interaction is contraindicated as P-gp inducers reduce sofosbuvir levels and its active metabolite (GS-331007), which is responsible for 90% of its pharmacologic effect. Fostamatinib increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via P-gp/BCRP inhibition. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp/BCRP substrate drugs and adjust dosages as necessary. Fostemsavir inhibits BCRP transporters, increasing ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels or effects. Avoid coadministration or modify the dose of BCRP substrates when used with fostemsavir. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via P-gp and BCRP inhibition. Monitor closely for potential interactions. Ibuprofen/famotidine decreases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels due to increased gastric pH. H2-receptor antagonists may be administered simultaneously or 12 hours apart from ledipasvir/sofosbuvir at doses not exceeding famotidine 40 mg twice daily. Istradefylline increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via P-gp inhibition. Consider dose reduction of sensitive P-gp substrates. Lansoprazole decreases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels due to increased gastric pH. PPI doses comparable to omeprazole 20 mg or less can be administered simultaneously with ledipasvir/sofosbuvir under fasted conditions. Lasmiditan, a BCRP inhibitor, increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels or effects. Avoid coadministration with BCRP substrates. Leniolisib, a BCRP inhibitor, increases systemic exposure to BCRP substrates. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Lonafarnib, a weak P-gp inhibitor, increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels. Monitor for adverse reactions and reduce P-gp substrate doses if needed. Magnesium oxide decreases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels due to increased gastric pH. Separate antacid and ledipasvir/sofosbuvir administration by 4 hours. Mavorixafor increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir levels via P-gp inhibition. Monitor mavorixafor closely and reduce its dose if needed. Momelotinib, a BCRP inhibitor, increases ledipasvir/sofosbuvir toxicity via plasma protein binding competition. Adjust doses of other BCRP substrates as necessary. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases naldemedine levels via P-gp inhibition. Monitor for potential adverse effects. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases nintedanib levels via P-gp inhibition. If adverse effects occur, manage with dose reduction, therapy interruption, or discontinuation.
